To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
geometric imperfections of PKMs lead to parasitic forces that cannot be controlled and that a modified computed torque scheme can be used to overcome this effect.
the control of redundantly actuated parallel manipulators is not affected by geometric uncertainties if the control forces are computed with respect to the nominal model.
the control of PKMs with actuation redundancy is affected by geometric imperfections, and that a novel control strategy is proposed that can overcome these problems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the control of redundant PKM in the presence of model uncertainties.
the control of redundant parallel manipulators in the presence of uncertainties, and the results can also be transferred to the control of redundant serial manipulators.
the control of redundant PKMs with geometric uncertainties, which is a challenging problem.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the control of PKMs can be achieved by means of standard model-based methods, if the PKM has no redundant actuators.
actuation redundancy is not beneficial for the control of PKMs, since the additional actuators are needed to compensate for geometric imperfections, and not for control purposes.
actuation redundancy is a double-edged sword: while it increases the robustness against model uncertainties, it also increases the sensitivity against geometric uncertainties.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
geometric uncertainties can be handled in a similar fashion as model uncertainties.
the control of PKMs with actuation redundancy is possible in the presence of uncertainties, but it requires a careful analysis of the control scheme.
geometric imperfections are not only a problem in terms of kinematic accuracy but can also lead to control problems that are not easily addressed with standard control schemes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
geometric uncertainties can be handled with model-based control schemes if actuation redundancy is not used.
the actuation redundancy is an important feature that should be taken into account when controlling PKM.
actuation redundancy can be a curse rather than a blessing for the control of PKMs.
